blocks.text: SYDNEY — Fiji and Tonga have declared that severe droughts fueled by the El Niño weather phenomenon are reaching crisis levels in the South Pacific. Drought in the region is strongly linked to the El Niño pattern, which dries up the rains that typically keep tropical islands lush and green. El Niño warms surface temperatures in parts of the Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in wind, heat and rain. The current El Niño is expected to become one of the most powerful on record, experts have warned. READ: ‘Very strong’ El Niño now active in tropical Pacific, says Pagasa The Fiji […]...
